rule: CSP draws panel text with the Windows default GUI font (GetStockObject(DEFAULT_GUI_FONT), registry GRE_Initialize GUIFont.Facename / GUIFont.Height), whatever CSP's UI language is. Pixel em = |height at 96 DPI| x capture DPI / 96.

tab.note: palette tab titles; measured only on this machine (Chinese Windows), not checked elsewhere

evidence: 2026-11-10 this machine (Windows display language zh-CN, DEFAULT_GUI_FONT = SimSun -12): 504 live panel captures at 144/168 DPI, GDI SimSun at 12*dpi/96 px matches panel text (NCC 0.91-0.94; YaHei 0.30-0.56).

2026-11-11 official manual screenshots (help.clip-studio.com, en/fr/de/es/ja/zh-tw editions, known labels only, 60-70 lines each): MS UI Gothic at 12 px is the best font in every edition (mean NCC ja 0.52, zh-tw 0.62, de 0.76, es 0.76, fr 0.70, en 0.48) against Tahoma/Segoe UI/Arial/MS Sans Serif 0.29-0.40 and JhengHei/YaHei/SimSun 0.23-0.30. MS UI Gothic is the default GUI font of Japanese Windows: the manual was shot on Japanese Windows for every language, so the UI font follows Windows, not CSP's language.

Not verified: Korean edition (no known label read in its screenshots), non-Chinese/Japanese Windows (the 'default' entry is the usual Western DEFAULT_GUI_FONT, MS Shell Dlg -> Tahoma/MS Sans Serif, unmeasured). PMingLiU, Gulim, Meiryo UI are not installed here.
